source_refs.note: Book p. 287: 11.1.1 Scalar Function, definition and the example f(t) = 3t + 2cos t

blocks.text: A scalar function is a function that assigns a single real number (a scalar) to each point in its domain. Think of it as a rule that assigns one value to a position in space, like measuring temperature at a specific point.

Mathematically, if to each value of a scalar variable \(t\) in the domain of a function \(f(t)\), there corresponds a unique scalar \(f\), then \(f\) is called a scalar function of \(t\). A real-valued function is commonly called a scalar function. For example, \(f(t) = 3t + 2\cos t\) is a scalar function.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"Scalar" means a quantity that has size only, no direction: mass, time, temperature, speed, length. A scalar function is a function whose OUTPUT is such a single real number.
Look at \(f(t) = 3t + 2\cos t\) in the table below: whatever \(t\) we put in, one real number comes out. Nothing in the answer has a direction, so \(f\) is a scalar function.

blocks.caption: Our table: each input t gives exactly one real number

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: To recognise a scalar function, look only at the output. One real number with no \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) and no angle brackets \(\langle\ \rangle\) means a scalar function. The number of inputs does not matter: the temperature \(T(x, y, z)\) at a point in space has three inputs but is still a scalar function (see 11.3.1).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. A scalar function assigns a single real number (a scalar) to each point of its domain.
2. If each value of \(t\) gives one unique scalar \(f\), then \(f\) is a scalar function of \(t\).
3. Real-valued function = scalar function; example: \(f(t) = 3t + 2\cos t\).
4. Temperature at a point is the everyday picture of a scalar function.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Calling a function "vector" because it has many inputs: scalar or vector depends on the output only.
2. Mixing up speed and velocity: speed (a number) is a scalar, velocity (number plus direction) is a vector.
3. Using degrees in \(\cos t\): \(\cos 0 = 1\) and \(\cos\pi = -1\) with \(t\) in radians.
